Chapter 6: Praying for Relationships and Community
Have you ever felt that quiet ache, watching someone you love search for their place in the world? For so many parents, there’s this constant hope that their adult children will find real, healthy relationships—deep friendships, caring mentors, maybe even a loving partner. Let’s be honest, life can feel isolating at times, and the right people truly do make all the difference.
Picture this: a mother sees her son, who’s just moved to a new city for work, struggling to settle in. The city feels huge, his office is a world of closed doors, and weekends? They just stretch on, lonely and quiet. She thinks back to his childhood—when friends were just a bike ride away—and wishes she could make it that easy again. But adulthood isn’t so simple, is it? Instead, she turns to prayer. She asks for doors to open, for genuine connections, for a sense of community to finally take root in his life.
Here’s something to pay attention to: it’s easy to overlook just how powerful relationships are in shaping our lives. Most of us don’t realize how that one true friend or a wise mentor can actually change the entire course of a season. As parents, it’s tough to stand on the sidelines—you want so badly to help, but you can’t just handpick the people your child meets. That’s where prayer steps in. It becomes this gentle way to ask for what you can’t arrange yourself—a loyal confidant, a supportive partner, even a wise guide.
I want to share another story—a father worried about his daughter’s circle of friends. He noticed she was drifting toward people who didn’t truly value her. Part of him wanted to step in, to give advice, maybe even a warning. But deep down, he knew that might only push her further away. So instead, he started to pray. He asked for discernment, for her to see her own worth, and for the right people to come into her life. Over time, something shifted. She began making different choices, naturally gravitating toward friends who encouraged her and helped her grow. That’s when the father realized—sometimes, prayers create space for change, even when words can’t.
Relationships, as you know, are rarely simple. They bring joy, but also pain; comfort, but sometimes challenge. Parents can’t choose friends or partners for their children, no matter how much they wish they could. But they can always pray—for wisdom, for protection from harm, for the courage to walk away from what isn’t right.
And maybe most importantly, they can ask for real community to form. For loneliness to finally lift. For love to blossom in the most unexpected places.
